prodigious: enormous, huge, far larger than ordinary things or people
hogsheads: very large casks or barrels used to hold liquids
packthread: strong thread or twine used for tying and binding bundles
scimitar: a short, curved sword with a single cutting edge
jerkin: a sleeveless leather or cloth jacket worn over other clothes
waistcoat: a sleeveless garment worn under a coat, like a vest
draught: a single drink or swallow of liquid
durst: dared; had the courage to do something
alighted: got down from a horse, carriage, or other vehicle
perspective: a telescope or spyglass for seeing distant objects
sublime: lofty, grand, and inspiring awe through great height or excellence
clemency: mercy shown by a ruler toward someone who deserves punishment
domestics: household servants who work inside a family's home
chairs: enclosed carrying seats borne on poles by servants
malice: a spiteful wish to hurt or harm other people
apprehended: seized or arrested; also meant understood or grasped
conjecture: a guess or opinion formed without firm proof
engine: a machine or mechanical device built for a purpose
cable: a very thick, strong rope, often used on ships
suffice: be enough or be sufficient for a purpose
pikes: long wooden spears with pointed iron heads used by soldiers
exiles: people forced to leave their own country as punishment
intercourse: communication, dealings, or social contact between people or nations
countenance: a person's face or the expression on it
wherein: in which; in what place or respect
whereupon: after which; at which point, upon which
wherewith: with which; by means of which
wherby: by which means; through which way
forbear: refrain from doing something; hold oneself back
descended: came down or went downward from a height
inclosed: shut in or surrounded by walls or fences
seamen: sailors who work on ships at sea
tongues: languages spoken by different peoples or nations
midst: the middle part or center of something
obliged: bound by duty, law, or gratitude to do something
thither: to that place; toward that particular spot
cutting: sharp and harsh in manner, or able to slice things
ointment: a soothing or healing cream rubbed onto the skin
linen: cloth woven from flax, used for shirts, sheets, and clothing
spectacles: eyeglasses worn to help the eyes see more clearly
pouch: a small bag or pocket hung from a belt
stool: a simple seat with legs and no back or arms
mathematicians: scholars skilled in numbers, measurement, and geometry
sexes: the two groups of males and females of a kind
posture: the way a person holds or positions the body
scabbard: a sheath that holds and protects a sword or blade
waded: walked through water or mud that is shallow
trial: a test of ability, or a formal hearing before a judge
heels: the back parts of shoes raised under the heel
fancy: imagination, or a whim or liking for something
mount: to climb onto a horse or to rise upward
dominions: lands and territories ruled over by a sovereign
magnificence: great splendor, grandeur, and impressive beauty or display
anchors: heavy hooked devices lowered to hold a ship in place
